analysis.title: What's Top of Mind in Macro Research: Continued yield pressures but equity resilience, Brazil elections, AI trends
key_insights: GS says the recent sharp widening in European sovereign credit spreads, particularly OAT-Bund, is beginning to set the boundaries for the bond selloff, even though G4 sovereign yields remain near multi-decade highs.
The widening in spreads has tightened financial conditions, which GS says should limit further rises in yields. GS sees a directional bias toward lower yields for both Bunds and US Treasuries.
GS forecasts only limited ECB and Fed tightening ahead, with both central banks likely to deliver their last rate hike of the cycle in December.
GS thinks the pressure from wider sovereign spreads on the Euro is nearing its limit and that the Euro is more likely than not to recover some of its recent losses in the coming weeks.
US equities have hit record highs on resilient earnings. GS expects the 3Q26 earnings season to deliver strong growth, with most companies again beating consensus.
Consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y for 3Q26, the highest heading into any reporting season since 2021.
European equities have also been supported by earnings. Higher rates are starting to bite, but continued earnings growth should remain supportive.
Brazil's presidential election goes to a likely competitive second-round runoff on October 25 after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected first-round win.
GS says a market-friendly election outcome that points to a tighter fiscal stance could lead USD/BRL to fall further to 4.50-4.80.

AI-related investment growth remains strong, as does US data center growth despite increased political scrutiny. Enterprise AI adoption among US establishments rose to 23.8% in September from 22.4% in August.
AI hardware investment is concentrated in the US and Asia, but the global investment boom is starting to generate positive growth spillovers in Europe, which GS expects to continue into 2027.

GS says China's export boom still has room to run over the next few years. Its future increasingly depends on foreign markets' ability to absorb additional Chinese supply, and it will eventually require stronger economic growth in importing countries.
earnings_insights: 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS growth: consensus expects +27% y/y (estimate, not yet reported), the highest heading into any reporting season since 2021. GS expects most companies to surpass consensus.
GS S&P 500 EPS forecasts from its table: $375 for 2026 (consensus $366) and $415 for 2027 (consensus $422), as estimates.

GS sees USD/BRL falling to this range if the runoff outcome is perceived as market-friendly and conducive to a tighter fiscal stance.
Adoption among US establishments continues to rise gradually.
